Thank you for installing Nooklin Photos.
Below you will find some very important information you SHOULD READ!
If you use the Hidden Section of this app, please read this carefully.

Why: photos you hide are stored privately on this device only, in a location only this app can read. That is what keeps them invisible to every other app on your phone. But that same privacy means Android permanently deletes them the moment this app is uninstalled — this is how your device handles all private app storage, not a bug, and it cannot be undone once it happens.

How to protect them: before you uninstall this app, or switch to a new device, open Settings > Hidden Section > Hidden Photos Backup and export a backup zip file to a location you control (for example another folder on your device, an SD card, or a cloud folder you manage yourself). This app will never do this automatically or without you asking — backing up is always your choice, on your terms.
I have read and acknowledge the information above.
We wish you happy use of the app!\nGreetings,\nNooklin Team

Everything Nooklin Photos does happens on this device. There is no server, no account, and no internet permission requested by this app at all, it is not technically able to send anything anywhere, even if it wanted to.
No analytics, no crash reporting, no usage tracking, no telemetry of any kind. This app does not know, and cannot find out, how you use it.
Machine Learning (face grouping, pet and object detection) runs entirely on your device using bundled models. Photos and any results are never uploaded anywhere.

Hidden items are moved into this app\'s own private storage, invisible to the system photo index and every other app on your phone. Exporting a Hidden Photos Backup, or sharing, printing or sending any photo to another app, only happens when you explicitly choose to, nothing is ever sent out automatically.

The Hidden Section is locked with your device\'s biometric or screen lock, and optionally an extra PIN. Hidden files are protected by that lock and by the app\'s private storage, they are not encrypted.
Edited photos and clips saved as new copies are new files on your device, and a trim you save on a video is stored only in this app\'s settings on this device, the video file itself is not changed.
The one notification this app can show (library scan complete) is generated and displayed entirely on your device, it is not a push notification and involves no server.

Nooklin Photos is provided free of charge, and \"as is,\" without warranty of any kind, express or implied, including, without limitation, any warranty that it will work correctly, be free of bugs, or be fit for any particular purpose.

To the fullest extent permitted by law, the developers of this app accept no liability for any loss or damage arising from its use, including but not limited to loss of photos, videos, or other data, however that loss occurs.

Data retention and backup are entirely your responsibility. Photos and videos you add to your device\'s regular library remain managed by Android\'s own MediaStore, as with any gallery app. Photos moved into this app\'s Hidden Section live in this app\'s own private storage, which is permanently deleted if the app is uninstalled, this app provides an export/backup tool for exactly this reason, and using it, on your own schedule, is on you.
Photos and videos you delete stay in Recently Deleted for 30 days and are then removed permanently. After that they cannot be restored by this app.
By using this app, you accept these terms and agree that you are solely responsible for your own data, backups, and how you use this app.
This text is provided as a general disclaimer and has not been reviewed by a lawyer for any specific jurisdiction.

On by default. Turns off the ability to share photos out of this app entirely, keeping Nooklin Photos a closed, private space with no way to send anything elsewhere. Turn this off if you want to be able to share photos.

When on (the default), sharing a photo removes the kinds of data chosen below, by default all four: location, camera and device, date and time, and description and other. When off, the original file is shared as-is, Exif data intact.

Location is the GPS position. Camera and device is the make, model, software, lens and capture settings. Date and time is when the photo was taken. Description and other is comments, author, copyright and other notes. With all four on, a JPEG loses all its metadata. With only some on, those kinds are removed and the rest stays. Videos lose all their metadata when at least one is on.

An extra layer of protection for the Hidden Section, separate from your device\'s own lock screen — you\'ll be asked for this PIN every time you open the Hidden Section, on top of, not instead of, the usual unlock.
When you set a PIN, a one-time recovery code is generated in case you forget it. It\'s shown once, right after setup — save it somewhere safe, since it can\'t be shown again.
When disabling Hidden Section, all data in the Hidden Section will remain there. Nothing is deleted and will be visible again after enabling Hidden Section again.
Sharing is turned off for the whole app (Settings > Sharing). Turn that back on first to change this setting.

When off (the default), the Hidden photo viewer has no Share button, so a hidden photo can\'t be shared out by mistake. Turning this on adds a Share button back to that viewer, same EXIF-stripped share behavior as your regular Library.
Hidden photos will be shareable to other apps again, using the same EXIF-stripped share behavior as your regular Library. Hidden photos still won\'t appear anywhere else on your device.

All photos and videos on your device. On Home, swipe the Library card left or right to browse everything, or tap Library to open the full grid. Tap an item to open the viewer: swipe left or right to move between items, pinch or double-tap to zoom and tap once to hide or show the controls. The filter menu shows All, Favorites, Videos or Screenshots and sorts newest or oldest first. Use the search button to find items by file name.

Create an album with the + button on the Albums screen. Add items from the viewer\'s ... menu or from the Library select menu with Add to Album. An album\'s menu lets you rename it, merge it into another album or delete it. Albums only group your items, the files themselves stay where they are.
Favorites, Recently Saved and Recently Deleted

Tap the heart in the viewer to make an item a favorite. Recently Saved shows items from the last 30 days. Items you delete go to Recently Deleted for 30 days, where you can recover them. After 30 days they are removed, and Android asks for your confirmation before files are permanently deleted.
Media Types and your Home screen

Home lists Videos, Panoramas, Screenshots, Screen Recordings, Slow Motion and RAW. Use Reorder Home Screen at the bottom of Home to change the order of sections and tiles, or to hide the ones you do not use.

Tap the edit button in the viewer. Photos can be rotated, flipped and cropped, and changed with Styles and Adjust (for example brightness, contrast, exposure, highlights and shadows). Tap the check mark to save. Videos open a trim editor. The ... menu also has Duplicate, which makes a copy of the item.

Share from the viewer\'s bottom bar. Copy in the ... menu puts the photo on the clipboard. In the Library, Select and then Share opens a share sheet for several items, with a row of apps that accept the share, Save to Folder, Export Unmodified Original and Copy. With one photo selected it also offers Print and Use as Wallpaper. Cancel stops a share that is still being prepared, for example a video. With Remove Exif data on, you choose in Settings > Sharing what is removed: Location, Camera and device, Date and time, and Description and other. All four are on by default.

App Lock asks for your device\'s own lock screen or biometric when you open the app. Disable Screenshots blocks screenshots and screen recording while you use the app.
What happens when you hide a photo or video

1. The file is copied into the app's private storage, together with a thumbnail.
2. Android asks your permission to delete the original from your phone.
3. If you allow it, the original is deleted and the app erases what it stored about it in your library: album and pet memberships, Machine Learning tags, face data and duplicate data. Favorites are not carried over.
4. If you decline, the hidden copy is discarded and nothing changes. If the copy fails, the original is never deleted.
Hiding several items at once shows one permission dialog for all of them. Whether an item is a screenshot, panorama, screen recording, slow motion or RAW is remembered, so it still shows under Media Types in the Hidden Section.
Hide is only available while the Hidden Section is on.
The item is written back to your phone\'s gallery as a new file and the hidden copy is removed. Albums, tags and face data it had before it was hidden are not restored.
What happens when you delete from the Hidden Section

The file stays private inside the app and is listed in the Hidden Section\'s own Recently Deleted for 30 days. It never shows up in your gallery or in the normal Recently Deleted. Restoring it from there puts it straight back in the Hidden Section, without any Android permission. After 30 days, or when you delete it for good, the file is erased from the app.
What happens when you delete a photo or video

The file itself is not touched. The app only lists it in Recently Deleted and hides it from the Library and albums. Recover brings it back at once. When you delete it for good from Recently Deleted, or when 30 days have passed, Android asks your permission and then removes the file from your phone. If you decline, the item returns to your Library.

Saving an edited photo creates a new JPEG photo next to the original. The original stays unchanged. For a video, Save Video keeps the file and only remembers where the trim starts and ends, while Save as New Clip cuts a new file.
Duplicate in the viewer\'s ... menu makes a copy of the file in your phone\'s gallery, with copy_ in front of the name.
Where the app keeps your choices

Favorites, albums, Recently Deleted entries and custom sort dates are stored inside the app, not in the photo files. Your photos are never changed by them. If you clear the app\'s data or uninstall it, these choices are lost.
What a Machine Learning scan does

A scan reads each photo on your device and saves only tags and numbers (such as face data) inside the app. Nothing leaves your phone. A later scan skips photos that have not changed. Turning Machine Learning off asks for confirmation and then deletes this data, and Clear analysis data does the same without turning it off.

The app makes a temporary copy of the photo or video and shares that copy. With Remove Exif data on, the kinds of data you chose in Settings > Sharing are removed from the copy. With all four on, a JPEG loses all its metadata without being compressed again, and a video is copied without its tags. With only some on, the chosen Exif tags are removed, and XMP and IPTC data also go when Location, Date and time or Description is on. A video loses all its metadata when at least one is on. The original is untouched. If removing fails, the file is not shared.

How the Hidden Section is locked

Opening the Hidden Section asks for your device\'s biometric or screen lock, and it locks again when you leave. An Extra PIN adds a second check. If you forget the PIN, the recovery code shown when you set it lets you choose a new PIN, and a new recovery code is made. After several wrong PIN guesses you have to wait before trying again. Hidden files are kept privately inside the app, so other apps cannot read them, but they are not encrypted.

Hidden files are deleted when the app is uninstalled, so Settings > Hidden Section > Hidden Photos Backup exports them to a zip file. The zip is a normal, unprotected file: anyone who gets it can open it, so keep it somewhere safe.
